world.title: 'Crimes against humanity' complaints filed against Bangladesh ex-president
world.summary: Complaints alleging "crimes against humanity" have been filed against former Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin shortly after his resignation. The complaints were submitted to the Bangladesh International Crimes Tribunal (ICT). Shahabuddin's tenure has been scrutinized, and these allegations add to ongoing concerns regarding accountability for past human rights violations in the country. The tribunal will review the complaints accordingly.

world.title: No path forward except jihad and resistance, Mojtaba Khamenei tells Hezbollah
world.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei praised Hezbollah, stating there is “no path forward except jihad and resistance.” He emphasized Tehran's commitment to supporting the group, labeling its defense as a strategic mandate. Khamenei called for the “absolute, unconditional termination” of Israeli aggression against Lebanon, reinforcing Iran's stance on the conflict and its backing of Hezbollah's actions.

world.title: Search for 17 missing crew after Vietnamese cargo ship sinks in South China Sea
world.summary: Search efforts are ongoing for 17 missing crew members after a Vietnamese cargo ship sank in the South China Sea due to bad weather. Rescuers from Vietnam, the Philippines, and China are participating in the multinational operation. The incident occurred near a Chinese-occupied shoal in the disputed region, highlighting ongoing tensions in the area.

business.title: She Was Laid Off Twice As an Immigrant; It Taught Her Resilience
business.summary: Tanvi Pisal, a 29-year-old UX designer from India, experienced two layoffs within a year while working in the US, prompting two cross-country moves in 2025. The layoffs significantly impacted her finances and mental health. This as-told-to essay recounts her journey and resilience, highlighting the challenges faced by immigrants in the workforce. The content has been edited for clarity.

business.title: Bain Capital in advanced talks for 25% stake in IndusInd Insurance, marking its first India insurance bet
business.summary: Bain Capital is in advanced negotiations to acquire a 25% stake in IndusInd General Insurance, potentially valuing the company at over 16,000 crore rupees. The private equity firm plans to invest between 4,000 and 5,000 crore rupees. Current discussions are centered on valuation and commercial terms, with the deal expected to be finalized by late August or early September.

business.title: Over 60 companies see MFs cut stakes for fourth straight quarter despite strong domestic inflows
business.summary: Over 60 listed companies have experienced mutual funds reducing their stakes for the fourth consecutive quarter, according to a Moneycontrol analysis. This trend persists despite mutual funds continuing to be strong buyers of Indian equities. The findings highlight a divergence between mutual fund investment strategies and their holdings in specific companies, reflecting broader market dynamics in the Indian equity landscape.

technology.title: US-Iran war news: Tehran signals it will pause attacks if America does the same; Trump shares AI images of Kharg strike, bombing of Iranian vessels - 10 KEY developments
technology.summary: The United States has paused airstrikes on Iran, indicating a potential shift towards diplomacy to prevent further regional conflict. Tehran has signaled it may also halt attacks if the U.S. does the same. Mediators emphasize that diplomatic solutions are essential for resolving the ongoing crisis. The situation remains tense, with both sides assessing their next moves.

technology.title: Palworld 1.0 surges to nearly 1 Million concurrent Steam players as sales Top 30 Million copies
technology.summary: Palworld's 1.0 launch achieved nearly one million concurrent players on Steam and sold approximately 1.8 million copies within the first ten days. Total sales have exceeded 30 million, generating nearly $700 million in revenue. The game maintains a 93% positive rating on Steam, reflecting its popularity since its early access release in early 2024.

technology.title: Claude AI Shared Chats Reportedly Exposed in Google Search Results
technology.summary: Anthropic's Claude AI shared links were found in public Google search results, leading to privacy concerns for users who had shared sensitive conversations. A Reddit post highlighted that hundreds of these chats were publicly accessible, prompting discussions about the implications for user confidentiality and data security. The incident raises questions regarding the handling of private information by AI platforms.

sports.title: Soumya recalled for Darwin Test after five-year absence
sports.summary: Bangladesh has announced a 15-player squad for their first Test in Australia in 23 years, with many players set to experience top-flight cricket in the country for the first time. Veteran batter Soumya Sarkar has been recalled after a five-year absence, as the team faces the challenge of missing three first-choice players due to injury.

sports.title: Commonwealth Games: Jadumani wins high-octane India-Pakistan bout, Preeti one win away from medal
sports.summary: Jadumani Singh defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman in a thrilling match at the Commonwealth Games boxing competition in Glasgow. Meanwhile, Preeti Pawar, an Asian Games bronze medallist, advanced to the quarterfinals with a commanding performance. Both athletes are now on track for potential medal wins, with Preeti just one victory away from securing her first Commonwealth Games medal.

sports.title: Commonwealth Games Day 4 Highlights: India end with four medals
sports.summary: On Day 4 of the Commonwealth Games, India secured four medals, including a silver from Rishikanta Singh in the men's 60kg weightlifting event. Singh lifted a Games record of 121 kg in the snatch and added 143 kg in the clean and jerk. This marks India's second medal at the Glasgow 2026 Games, following Jhandu Kumar's bronze.

health.title: Researchers identify eight new genes linked to schizophrenia
health.summary: Researchers in the United Kingdom have identified eight new genes linked to schizophrenia, a complex psychiatric disorder characterized by symptoms like hallucinations and delusions. This discovery enhances the understanding of the condition and may aid in developing future treatments. Schizophrenia significantly impacts how individuals think, feel, and behave, highlighting the importance of ongoing research in this area.

health.title: Sleep Disorders Don’t Just Exhaust You. New Research Shows They Change Your Brain
health.summary: Research from Florida International University indicates that sleep disorders lead to both shared and unique structural changes in brain systems responsible for attention, decision-making, and emotional regulation. These alterations can have significant implications beyond mere fatigue, affecting cognitive functions and emotional control. The findings highlight the importance of addressing sleep disorders to mitigate their impact on brain health.

health.title: US FDA nod for 1st pill to replace jabs to fight high cholesterol
health.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved the world's first oral PCSK9 inhibitor, offering patients with difficult-to-control high cholesterol an alternative to injectable treatments. This new pill aims to help manage cholesterol levels more conveniently, potentially changing the treatment landscape for those struggling with high cholesterol. The approval marks a significant advancement in cholesterol management options.

science.title: Fertility and IVF facility relaunched at Manipal Hospital
science.summary: Manipal Hospital Mysuru relaunched its Fertility and IVF Centre on World IVF Day, enhancing its services with upgraded technology and improved infrastructure. The facility now offers a broader range of advanced reproductive treatments. The relaunch event featured Rtn. Sam Cherian, Founder-Chairman of Schevaran Laboratories, and DCP (Law and Order) Dr. Harsha Priyamvada, highlighting the hospital's commitment to fertility care.

science.title: From The Hindu Archives, July 27, 1976: ‘Roman letter’ on Mars rock
science.summary: On July 26, 1976, U.S. scientists successfully transmitted commands to Mars, resolving an issue with the Viking lander's soil-sampling arm. However, another critical experiment involving the seismology probe faced challenges that could not be addressed from Earth. The developments were reported from Pasadena, California, highlighting ongoing efforts in Mars exploration and the complexities of remote scientific operations.

science.title: Scientists trace the shocking origin of human eyes to an ancient "cyclops": Study
science.summary: Researchers have identified a tiny, one-eyed ancestor from nearly 600 million years ago as a key influence in the evolution of vertebrate eyes, including humans. This ancient organism's median eye is believed to have evolved into the pineal gland, which plays a crucial role in regulating sleep patterns in relation to daylight.
